title: Remote wait drops the session request id used for frontend correlation
reasoning: RemoteToolBase centralizes request id selection from ctx.session.metadata so a backend remote stub can correlate the frontend execution result with the active request. RemoteWaitTool bypasses that helper by always passing a fresh UUID, unlike sibling remote tools, so any caller that supplied a request_id in session metadata will receive a RemoteToolResult that cannot be matched to the original request id. That is especially risky because wait is described as returning a delayed status and fresh screen image, so lost correlation can strand or misattribute the asynchronous frontend response.
recommendation: Remove the explicit request_id override in RemoteWaitTool so it uses _build_remote_result's default _get_request_id behavior, or only generate a new id when no session request_id exists and document why wait requires a distinct child id.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for request id propagation across remote tool stubs, and the inconsistency is visible only by comparing RemoteWaitTool to the base contract.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend unit test that runs RemoteWaitTool with a ToolContext containing session.metadata.request_id and asserts the returned RemoteToolResult.request_id preserves that value, alongside one sibling tool for parity.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/tools/remote_tools/computer.py and a focused remote tool request-id test.
